STRENGTHENED - the degenerate fixture is not only statistically meaningless, it may be the ONLY configuration that fits inside the gate.

The gate is running now. Live measurement, mid-run:

  fixture ready signal   11:36:52
  observed at            11:51:36
  measured phase elapsed 14 min 44 s          against a 30-minute gate  (49% consumed)
  worker process RSS     2,545,328 KB = 2.43 GiB   against a 4 GiB gate (61% consumed)
  worker CPU time        12 min 26 s

Caveat: 2.43 GiB is process RSS; the gate scores INCREMENTAL RSS above a post-gc baseline, so the scored figure will be lower. The elapsed figure is directly comparable.

That is roughly half the time budget and a majority of the memory budget spent on the most favourable configuration the harness can present: q = 2, three partitions, six ordered edges, and a local covariance that is singular for 84% of supports.

INTERACTION WITH THE FIX I RECOMMENDED

Both remedies multiply the dominant cost:
  observations 32 -> 200   residual accumulation is n * k^2 per support, so about 6x
  partitions   3 -> 6      30 ordered edges instead of 6, about 5x, plus 2x residual accumulation

Either would place the run far outside 30 minutes. So the honest reading is that dense local shrinkage at whole-brain scale does NOT fit the gate at any statistically meaningful setting, and the current fixture passes only because it is degenerate.

THIS IS ALREADY ANTICIPATED IN YOUR OWN ACCEPTANCE

"If dense local shrinkage misses the gate, version 0.1 supports brain-scale diagonal metrics and explicitly scopes dense metrics to smaller supports/node sets."

That clause looks like the correct outcome rather than a contingency. Recommend the epic conclude with an explicit scope statement - brain-scale diagonal metrics supported, dense local metrics scoped to a declared node count or support size - and that the gate be re-run at a non-degenerate fixture to find where the real boundary sits, rather than reporting a pass at settings where no searchlight can estimate a covariance.

I will report the completed gate numbers once the run finishes.
